crore for liquidating his sharesin
a pharmaceutical company

JUSTMONTHS before a 72-yearold man in Mumbaifell preytoa Rs 58-crore digital arrest scam, one of the largest cyber cons in the country, he received Rs 50 crore for liquidating his sharesin a pharmaceutical company where he was a partner, The Indian Express has learnt. While the money came into his account "earlier this year", officers associated with the probe told this newspaper, the man was first contacted via video call by digital scamsters on August 19. Subsequently, sources said, the scamsters forced the victim to visit four banks where he held accounts for 27 days across a40- day period to transfer money to various "mule accounts" while they listened in on an "active phone call" to "keep a tab".

Her aim has been to ensure that children with diarrhoea do not end upconsuming flavoured, sweet-ened beverages in place of the genuine Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS), a landmark discovery in medicine pioneered by Dr Dilip Mahalanabis. On Wednesday, the country's food regulator issued an order banning all beverages from using the term ORS in their trade-marked name, withdrawing an earlier order allowing the term with disclaimers. Over the last decade or so, several tetra-pack products claiming to be ORS have entered the market without actually adhering to the sugar and salt ratios needed fora person to effectively absorb the water they are drinking, Dr Santhosh told The Indian Express. Her journey started with educating people on social media around eight years ago - she saw children coming to her clinics who were severely dehydrated despite being given what the parents assumed was an ORS solution. But she knew that was not enough. These products were not only giving children excess sugar, they were actively harming their health. "Even if a product carries the warming 'not ORS - which many of the new products do not - people still think
